I will keep it simple this year. I am 73, so I will not spread myself across many crops that need a lot of hand work or constant watching. In Quzhou, the most familiar and steady path for me is still the winter wheat and summer maize rotation. It fits the local weather, the land, the machines, and the way I know how to farm. The county is a wheat-maize area, spring is often dry and windy, and rain is mostly in summer, so this rotation matches the season better than chasing fancier cash crops.

I will put all my land into grain. I will not plant cotton or vegetables. Cotton drags on too long and vegetables are too tiring for me, with too much daily management and selling trouble. Grain is easier to manage, easier to hire machine work for, and safer for an older man like me. I will use improved winter wheat seed and hybrid summer maize seed, because I want stable emergence and stable yield, not the trouble of saving old seed.

For the wheat, I will keep fertilizer moderate and not push too hard. I do not want waste, lodging, or too much cost. I will plough before wheat so the straw can go down and the soil stays looser. I will water a few times only when the crop really needs it, because spring here is dry but water also costs money. I will spray only as needed for weeds, rust, aphids, and later for maize pests, but I will not spray blindly. After wheat harvest, I will quickly plant summer maize on the same land. For maize, I will keep management simple, use rotary tillage after wheat, put on enough fertilizer for steady growth, and aim for a solid yield instead of gambling on a record.
